# zlaesy

> Compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a 2-by-2 complex symmetric matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlaesy from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlaesy';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlaesy( a, b, c, rt1, rt2, evscal, cs1, sn1 ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `Complex128` | The (1,1) element of the input matrix |
| `b` | `Complex128` | The (1,2) and (2,1) element of the input matrix |
| `c` | `Complex128` | The (2,2) element of the input matrix |
| `rt1` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of larger modulus |
| `rt2` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of smaller modulus |
| `evscal` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the complex value by which the eigenvector matrix was scaled to make it orthonormal |
| `cs1` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `cs1` |
| `sn1` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): if EVSCAL .NE |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: The ( 1, 1 ) element of input matrix.
- `b`: The ( 1, 2 ) element of input matrix. The ( 2, 1 ) element is also given by B, since the 2-by-2 matrix is symmetric.
- `c`: The ( 2, 2 ) element of input matrix.
- `rt1`: The eigenvalue of larger modulus.
- `rt2`: The eigenvalue of smaller modulus.
- `evscal`: The complex value by which the eigenvector matrix was scaled to make it orthonormal. If `EVSCAL` is zero, the eigenvectors were not computed. This means one of two things: the 2-by-2 matrix could not be diagonalized, or the norm of the matrix of eigenvectors before scaling was larger than the threshold value THRESH (set below).
- `sn1`: If $\mathrm{EVSCAL} \ne 0$, ( `CS1`, `SN1` ) is the unit right eigenvector for `RT1`.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlaesy.ndarray(
    a, b, c,
    rt1, offsetRt1,
    rt2, offsetRt2,
    evscal, offsetEvscal,
    cs1, offsetCs1,
    sn1, offsetSn1
) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `Complex128` | The (1,1) element of the input matrix |
| `b` | `Complex128` | The (1,2) and (2,1) element of the input matrix |
| `c` | `Complex128` | The (2,2) element of the input matrix |
| `rt1` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of larger modulus |
| ↳ `offsetRt1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `rt1` (in complex elements) |
| `rt2` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the eigenvalue of smaller modulus |
| ↳ `offsetRt2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `rt2` (in complex elements) |
| `evscal` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the complex value by which the eigenvector matrix was scaled to make it orthonormal |
| ↳ `offsetEvscal` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `evscal` (in complex elements) |
| `cs1` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `cs1` |
| ↳ `offsetCs1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `cs1` (in complex elements) |
| `sn1` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): if EVSCAL .NE |
| ↳ `offsetSn1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `sn1` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: The ( 1, 1 ) element of input matrix.
- `b`: The ( 1, 2 ) element of input matrix. The ( 2, 1 ) element is also given by B, since the 2-by-2 matrix is symmetric.
- `c`: The ( 2, 2 ) element of input matrix.
- `rt1`: The eigenvalue of larger modulus.
- `rt2`: The eigenvalue of smaller modulus.
- `evscal`: The complex value by which the eigenvector matrix was scaled to make it orthonormal. If `EVSCAL` is zero, the eigenvectors were not computed. This means one of two things: the 2-by-2 matrix could not be diagonalized, or the norm of the matrix of eigenvectors before scaling was larger than the threshold value THRESH (set below).
- `sn1`: If $\mathrm{EVSCAL} \ne 0$, ( `CS1`, `SN1` ) is the unit right eigenvector for `RT1`.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zlaesy()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLAESY`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlaesy.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import zlaesy from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlaesy';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';

// Using the standard interface:
const rt1 = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const rt1v = reinterpret( rt1, 0 );
const rt2 = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const rt2v = reinterpret( rt2, 0 );
const evscal = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const evscalv = reinterpret( evscal, 0 );
const cs1 = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const cs1v = reinterpret( cs1, 0 );
const sn1 = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const sn1v = reinterpret( sn1, 0 );

zlaesy( 1, 1, 1.0, rt1, rt2, evscal, cs1, sn1 );
let out = {
	'rt1r': rt1v[ 0 ],
	'rt1i': rt1v[ 1 ],
	'rt2r': rt2v[ 0 ],
	'rt2i': rt2v[ 1 ],
	'evscalr': evscalv[ 0 ],
	'evscali': evscalv[ 1 ],
	'cs1r': cs1v[ 0 ],
	'cs1i': cs1v[ 1 ],
	'sn1r': sn1v[ 0 ],
	'sn1i': sn1v[ 1 ]
};
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
zlaesy.ndarray( 1, 1, 1.0, rt1, 0, rt2, 0, evscal, 0, cs1, 0, sn1, 0 );
out = {
	'rt1r': rt1v[ 0 ],
	'rt1i': rt1v[ 1 ],
	'rt2r': rt2v[ 0 ],
	'rt2i': rt2v[ 1 ],
	'evscalr': evscalv[ 0 ],
	'evscali': evscalv[ 1 ],
	'cs1r': cs1v[ 0 ],
	'cs1i': cs1v[ 1 ],
	'sn1r': sn1v[ 0 ],
	'sn1i': sn1v[ 1 ]
};
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLAESY`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLAESY computes the eigendecomposition of a 2-by-2 symmetric matrix

( ( A, B );( B, C ) )

provided the norm of the matrix of eigenvectors is larger than some threshold value.

`RT1` is the eigenvalue of larger absolute value, and `RT2` of smaller absolute value. If the eigenvectors are computed, then on return ( `CS1`, `SN1` ) is the unit eigenvector for `RT1`, hence

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS1} & \mathrm{SN1} \\ -\mathrm{SN1} & \mathrm{CS1} \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} A & B \\ B & C \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CS1} & -\mathrm{SN1} \\ \mathrm{SN1} & \mathrm{CS1} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{RT1} & 0 \\ 0 & \mathrm{RT2} \end{bmatrix}
$$

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
